{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Deerskin / HDI Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Contract review findings — verified issues, walk-away items and next steps

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed EXHIBIT 10.2 against our playbook. The agreement is materially unbalanced against us in its risk-allocation architecture: it contains **no indemnification, no IP ownership allocation, no limitation of liability, no performance warranty, no exit/transition mechanics and no insurance obligation**. In practical terms, HDI designs, hosts and operates the Site and holds our Content, user information and order data, yet nothing in the document allocates ownership of those assets, requires their return, caps either party's exposure, or backs HDI's performance with a warranty or insurance.

Separately, several clauses that do exist impose one-sided burdens on us. Section 6.1 binds the Company (not HDI) to full-term exclusivity over Deerskin Products and "substantially similar" products, and hands HDI the exclusive right to use our own "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site — with no performance exit and only a closeout-merchandise carve-out (§ 6.2). Section 4.2 charges us an uncapped Termination Payment (half of twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly instalments) whenever we terminate, while Section 4.1 gives us no express mid-term convenience exit and requires 90 days' notice to avoid auto-renewal. Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns sentence with no assignment mechanics, leaving HDI free to assign to a Deerskin competitor.

Three areas are clean and require no redline: no MFN obligation burdens us (indeed § 1.8 runs a "no less favourably" promotion obligation in our favour), there is no minimum purchase or volume commitment (§ 3.1 is a pure revenue share above an $11,000 monthly threshold), and there is no non-solicitation covenant binding us. Section 6.3 (HDI's two-year covenant) and § 3.4's cost and notice terms also favour us and are left intact.

In total: **19 findings — 3 critical, 6 high, 7 medium, 2 low; 3 compliant, 10 deviations, 6 missing.** Four findings sit in walk-away territory (indemnification, Company exclusivity/non-compete, insurance) and should be treated as non-negotiable gating items.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 (insert new § 9A) | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere; § 9 stops at the Globix acknowledgement and § 10 moves to General Provisions. No HDI IP indemnity at all — walk-away. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 (insert new § 5.5) | No IP ownership provision. § 5.2 gives us only artistic/editorial control; the only grant runs the other way (our "Deerskin" Marks to HDI at § 6.1). Fails preferred and fallback. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 | No cap or damages exclusion; "liability" appears only in the No Joint Venture clause (§ 10.2). Both parties face unlimited exposure. Inserted at fallback: mutual 12-months'-fees cap with Excluded Claims. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 10.3 (per § 5.4 anchor) | Bare successors-and-assigns clause; no affiliate/successor right for us, no consent gate on HDI, HDI free to assign to a Deerskin competitor. No change-of-control termination right elsewhere. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 6.1 (per § 5.4 anchor) | We are barred from any similar Internet project for Deerskin or substantially similar products, and HDI gains the exclusive right to our own brand. Runs the full auto-renewing term (§ 4.1) with no performance exit — walk-away. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 4.2 (per § 1.4 anchor) | Termination Payment of half of twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly instalments, uncapped and untethered to fees. Fallback cure: new § 4.2(d) capping at three months' § 3.1 fees as sole liquidated amount. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | Access/use rights run to "the Company" alone and § 10.3 confirms no other person acquires rights, so affiliates are excluded. Successor element already satisfied; no at-will revocation right, so not walk-away. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation *(verification: repaired)* | § 6.1 (per § 5.4 anchor) | Open-ended "substantially similar" scope expressly extended to companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled; no 12-month cap given auto-renewal; no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. Fails four of five fallback elements. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation *(verification: repaired)* | § 4.1 / § 4.2 (per § 1.4 anchor) | § 4.1 is a non-renewal mechanic only; we have no mid-term convenience exit, while HDI's notice may fix any Termination Date and exit mid-term. Cure lands at fallback (90 days' notice; HDI confined to end of term; payment capped at three months). |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 (per § 1.4 anchor) | Notice (30 days) and cost (HDI bears all fees) already exceed fallback and inspection is confined to payment records with no system access, but frequency is unlimited. Cure: once-per-year cap. |
| 11 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | **Compliant** | § 1.4 | No MFN obligation on us across §§ 3, 6 and 7. The only "no less favorably" mechanic (§ 1.8) runs in our favour at HDI's cost. Preferred position; no redline. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume | **Compliant** | § 1.4 | § 3.1 is a pure 30% revenue share above an $11,000 monthly threshold; §§ 3.2–3.4 are timing, reconciliation and audit mechanics. No minimum, shortfall or take-or-pay. Preferred position. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Compliant** | § 5.4 | § 5.4 is a General Manager liaison appointment only; no hiring restriction anywhere. Incidental "employees/agents" references at §§ 8.1(c) and 10.2 impose no covenant. Preferred position. |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 4.1 (per § 1.4 anchor) | Successive one-year renewals are acceptable, but the 90-day non-renewal notice exceeds the 60-day fallback maximum. Fee is fixed at 30% of Net Sales with no uplift mechanic, so the price-cap element is not engaged. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 (insert § 4.3) | § 4 covers only term, notice and the Termination Payment. No transition assistance, no data return or export, no controlled deletion — despite HDI holding our Content, user information and order data. |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Missing | § 5.4 (insert § 9(c)) | § 9 is limited to mutual authority representations and the Globix acknowledgement. No warranty of development, hosting or Site software, no duration, no remedy (and no "AS IS" disclaimer either). |
| 17 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 10.5 (per § 5.4 anchor) | New York law is our preferred governing law, but there is no venue, jurisdiction or arbitration provision anywhere, so the exclusive-jurisdiction element fails. Governing law sentence untouched. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 (insert § 10.9) | No insurance provision; General Provisions end at Headings/Counterparts. HDI hosts the Site on its own server and accesses our Content and user data (§ 8.1), so the rule applies — walk-away absent coverage. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These four items fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be resolved before signature:

1. **No HDI indemnification (INDEMN, critical).** There is no indemnity of any kind. We require a new § 9A under which HDI defends and indemnifies the Company and its affiliates for third-party IP infringement, HDI's breach of law, HDI-caused data breaches and HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and a reciprocal Company indemnity narrowed to the Content we supply and our own breach of law.
2. **Company-side exclusivity and non-compete (EXCLUSIVITY / NONCOMPETE, high).** § 6.1 imposes exclusive dealing on us for the full auto-renewing term with no performance-based exit — § 1.6 offers only a discretionary right if the Site is late, and the § 6.2 closeout carve-out does not cure it. It also hands HDI the exclusive right to use our own "Deerskin" brand. We seek the preferred cure: replace § 6.1 with a clause-level no-restriction statement scoped to Article 6, preserving § 6.2, § 6.3 (which benefits us) and the § 9(b) Globix wind-down proviso.
3. **No insurance (INSURANCE, low severity but walk-away in substance).** HDI processes our data with no coverage behind it. We require § 10.9: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M where HDI processes any Company data, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request.
4. **No data return on exit (TRANSITION, medium).** The absence of any data-return obligation risks the walk-away outcome of losing our Content, user information and order data entirely. We require § 4.3: up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of all Company data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion after return.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the three critical gaps (indemnity § 9A, IP ownership § 5.5, mutual 12-months'-fees liability cap) plus the four inserted clauses (§ 4.1A convenience termination, § 4.2(d) fee cap, § 4.3 transition, § 9(c) warranty, § 10.9 insurance) and the short amendments to §§ 1.4, 3.4, 4.1, 10.3 and 10.5.
2. **Front-load the walk-away items** in the covering note so HDI understands that indemnity, § 6.1 exclusivity, insurance and data return are gating rather than trading positions.
3. **Signal our fallbacks where sensible.** On IP we can accept the fallback (HDI retains generic tools and know-how against a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables) if HDI resists assignment. On liability, liquidated damages, termination for convenience, audit frequency, renewal notice and warranty we have already drafted at the fallback and have no further room.
4. **Confirm commercial appetite on § 4.2.** The cap at three months of § 3.1 fees materially changes our exit economics; the deal team should confirm this is the right ask before we send.
5. **Note the two "repaired" findings** (NONCOMPETE, T4C) — we will re-verify the final language of those two inserts against §§ 4.1, 4.2 and 6.1–6.3 before release to confirm no cross-reference conflict.
6. **No action required** on MFN, minimum commitments or non-solicitation; we will confirm in the covering note that these are accepted as drafted so HDI does not reopen them.

---

*Prepared from verified findings only. No section reference or conclusion beyond the supplied findings has been added.*"}
